_why: URL fragments a human rejected after looking at the image. The automated guards cannot catch these: each is a sharp, correctly sized picture of the right product that is still wrong for a storefront gallery. Matching on a fragment rather than a whole URL survives the query strings these CDNs append. Without this list, every re-run downloads them again and the eye check has to be redone from scratch.

_note_on_depth: Galaxy S26 Ultra stops at three images on purpose. Its buy page has no fourth clean product shot -- every remaining candidate is marketing artwork. Three verified images beat four with one wrong in it, and ProductPage probes each path and renders only what resolves.
_note_on_xiaomi: mi.com's global product pages are long-scroll marketing pages with no clean PDP gallery -- every candidate is art-directed with burnt-in type. Xiaomi is the slice's tier-1 failure and falls through to the Commons/Unsplash ladder, which is what the ladder is for.
_note_on_wrong_generation: New failure mode found in the phones slice: the Commons fallback returned genuine, sharp, correctly branded photographs of a Xiaomi 15 Ultra for a Xiaomi 17 Ultra listing -- one of them showing the model name on screen. Every existing guard passed, because the subject really is a Xiaomi phone. allowBrands made it worse by confirming the brand while ignoring the generation. A tier-2 seed must name the same model as the listing; when Commons has no photograph of that model, the product keeps fewer verified images rather than borrowing last year's.
